depth_targets.title: HTTP, Pub/Sub and App Engine HTTP targets
limitations: A Pub/Sub target is delivered into Vyomi's Pub/Sub core for real on every substrate — a subscriber receives an actual message.

On Nano (and the dev server) there is no outbound network path, so an HTTP target is recorded as attempted only (lastAttemptTime/status are stamped; the target URL is never actually invoked). The offline appliance really sends the request (method, headers, body), retries it per retryConfig, and maps the real response code onto the job's status.
App Engine HTTP targets are recorded as attempted (lastAttemptTime/status stamped) on every substrate; Vyomi doesn't model App Engine, so the relative URL is never dispatched anywhere.

OAuth and OIDC auth headers are stored and returned to the SDK exactly as configured; the offline appliance sends a placeholder bearer token rather than minting or verifying a real one for the configured service account.

depth_targets.title: App Engine cron jobs (legacy cron.yaml)
limitations: App Engine isn't modeled in Vyomi, so the legacy cron.yaml-based jobs the real console lists under this tab have no backend to read from.
